source.title: Teacher Geometry Shapes Learnability in Teacher-Student Networks
source.authors: Kai J. Sandbrink; Flavio Martinelli; Alexander van Meegen; W. Gerstner; Johanni Brea

record.file_problem: No apparent text corruption or truncation; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains randomly initialized shallow student networks by gradient flow to match teacher outputs, then measures convergence to zero loss. This tests learnability and optimization failure in a teacher-student setting, but not the benchmark classification recipes specified in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own global-minimum success rates and local-minimum outcomes. It does not test CIFAR classification, depth or shortcuts, activation-matched initialization comparisons, above-stability learning rates, or batch normalization. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The equal-width ReLU teacher-student sweep directly tests V2's component that optimization failures become more frequent as teacher and student grow together. Section 3.2 explicitly reports decreasing global-minimum success with increasing width. The setting differs through trainable readouts and biases, finite data, and gradient flow followed by second-order optimization. Extra student neurons are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that teacher geometry and student initialization jointly shape global-minimum success, maximally dissimilar teachers are generally easiest, and faster readout learning with slower inner-bias learning improves success by reducing OOB failures. They also emphasize that initial overlap does not explain interior-minimum outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses one-hidden-layer teacher-student regression with gradient flow and squared loss on Gaussian inputs, measuring convergence to zero output-matching loss. It does not use benchmark image classification or the recipes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Teacher distribution and geometry, teacher readout signs, input dimensionality, number of teacher nodes, initial student-teacher similarity and readout sign, inner bias and readout learning speeds, and optimizer affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Global-minimum success depends strongly on teacher geometry, readout signs, input dimensionality, and single-neuron starting alignment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In shallow teacher-student regression, teacher structure and student initialization substantially affect the probability of reaching zero squared loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher distributions differ in their balance of OOB and interior minima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Teacher geometry and readout signs affect which optimization failure modes occur in finite-data shallow ReLU regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Faster readout learning combined with slower inner-bias learning improves success; Adam does not improve success over the reported gradient-flow baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-specific learning speeds can improve global-minimum success in these shallow teacher-student networks, while switching to Adam does not resolve OOB failures.

record.problems: The results concern shallow teacher-student squared-loss fitting, not benchmark classification. Exact rates for many outcomes are shown only in figures and are not stated in the text. Runs that did not generate files were excluded; saved runs were analyzed without an additional convergence criterion. Larger settings had incomplete runs within the stated time limit.
record.rows_left_out: No figure-only numeric values were transcribed. Table 1 contains convergence counts, but its flattened layout does not reliably preserve all distribution-to-value mappings; no numbers were assigned from it. Cited prior-work results were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Convolutional CIFAR classification, random or corrupted labels, and the specified size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.

Whether one or two extra student neurons sharply reduce failures; the exact original recipe and full 6–20-neuron range. The study tests matched widths 2, 4, 8, and 16 under a different optimization procedure.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh initialization, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a stability threshold, transient loss growth, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. For unlinked rows, cannot_determine refers to the named claim versions, not to whether the reported finding exists. Exact figure values were explicitly declared left out, so they are not listed as missing. Width-dependent failures require caution: unfinished runs were excluded, saved runs had no additional convergence filter, and the optimization included second-order refinement. The paper contains conflicting descriptions of the two-neuron angle trend.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 classification, corrupted or random classification labels, SGD or Adam benchmark recipe, or comparison of model size, early stopping, and regularization as described.

The main experiments use student and teacher networks of equal width (ρ = 1); the study does not compare matched widths with students one or two neurons wider, nor report spurious-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow together.
No deep plain versus residual network comparison, batch normalization, ImageNet or CIFAR classification, or special initialization for deep plain networks.

The study does not compare activation-matched, Gaussian, or orthogonal initializations or test trainable depth. Glorot initialization appears in some experiments but is not compared against other initialization schemes.
No learning-rate sweep around a stability threshold, curvature tracking, or sharpness measurement.
No batch-normalization comparison or Fixup recipe.

rows.subject: student networks (teacher and student width M = N; ρ = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-flow training to match teacher-generated outputs; success classified by final loss below 10⁻¹⁸.

conditions.value: M and D sweeps; text says success falls as M increases and rises as D increases

rows.measure: Fraction of student fits reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Standard and minimally dissimilar teacher distributions; exact values are not stated in the Results text.
rows.value: The maximally dissimilar distribution has the highest success rates in almost all simulations; success decreases with increasing teacher nodes and increases with input dimensionality. Similar qualitative results are reported for softplus and tanh.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in figures; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: Textual aggregate across tested settings; exact per-setting rates are presented in figures and Table 1.
rows.check: Link only the ReLU width sweep at D = 2 to V2; separate the dimensionality sweep and softplus/tanh results. Success decreases as matched teacher/student width increases. Training includes second-order refinement after gradient flow, and unsuccessful saved runs are not all independently verified local minima.

Keep other activations and the dimensionality sweep separate.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU student networks
rows.size_stated: 2 student neurons; D = 2 in analytical setting
rows.stage_stated: gradient flow; analytical setting assumes fast readout weights and infinite Gaussian data
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed loss landscapes and trajectories as teacher readout signs and inter-neuron angle varied.

conditions.value: θ⋆ swept from π/16 to π in 16 steps

rows.measure: Whether trajectories reach global or non-global minima
rows.value: Mixed-sign teachers have local minima and a nonzero fraction of trajectories is trapped at all tested angles; same-sign teachers have no trapped trajectories in the analytical setting.
rows.note: Analytical loss-landscape result, not a benchmark classification experiment.
rows.check: The two-neuron analytical landscape with fast readouts and grid initializations does not measure V2's width trend or benefit from extra neurons.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU student networks
rows.stage_stated: finite-data gradient flow with Glorot-initialized weights
rows.operation_detail: Varied the angle between the two teacher neurons and measured student convergence.
rows.measure: Fraction of students reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Teacher angle θ⋆ = 0; exact rate not stated.
rows.value: As θ⋆ grows, a larger fraction of students get stuck in local minima above the global minimum, except for perfectly parallel hyperplanes at θ⋆ = 0.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in figure; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The result concerns teacher geometry and finite-data shallow-network fitting.
rows.check: This fixed-width geometry sweep does not measure V2's width effects. Its direction is also internally inconsistent: Section 4.2 says failure increases with angle, whereas Appendix F.5 says success increases toward opposite directions. The figure values are unavailable here to resolve this.

rows.subject: two-neuron ReLU student networks
rows.stage_stated: finite-data gradient flow with Glorot-initialized weights
rows.operation_detail: Compared success for same-sign and opposite-sign teacher readouts while varying teacher geometry.
rows.measure: Fraction of students reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Opposite-sign teacher readouts; exact rate not stated.
rows.value: For same-sign teachers, success is slightly smaller than for opposing signs, contrary to the analytical setting where same-sign trajectories all reach the global minimum.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in figure; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The text describes the finite-data comparison qualitatively.
rows.check: The fixed two-neuron readout-sign comparison does not measure a claimed width effect. Preserve its analytical-versus-finite-data distinction as a separate geometry finding.

rows.subject: student networks across teacher distributions
rows.operation_detail: Classified fitted students by global, out-of-bounds (OOB), and interior minima.

conditions.value: maximally dissimilar versus standard and minimally dissimilar

rows.measure: Frequency of OOB and interior minima among student outcomes
rows.baseline: Standard and minimally dissimilar teacher distributions; exact frequencies not stated in prose.
rows.value: Maximally dissimilar teachers produce fewer OOB neurons and more interior minima than the other teacher types.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of mean across eight settings shown in figure; exact values not stated.
rows.note: This classifies failure modes rather than reporting benchmark classification error.
rows.check: Minima-type frequencies aggregated across widths and dimensionalities do not establish the width dependence named by V2. Distinguish the fraction of networks in OOB minima from counts of OOB neurons.

rows.subject: student networks on modified teacher distributions
rows.size_stated: ρ = 1; M and D settings as in main experiments
rows.operation_detail: Changed teacher readout-sign patterns while holding the distribution family’s geometry as described.

conditions.value: maximally dissimilar with same readout signs; minimally dissimilar with evenly matched signs

rows.measure: Student success rate at reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Maximally dissimilar teachers with mixed signs and minimally dissimilar teachers with same signs.
rows.value: Changing signs has a large impact, but neither modified distribution is as successful as the maximally dissimilar distribution; both are only slightly above minimally dissimilar teachers.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars represent standard error of the binomial proportion in Figure 11; exact values not stated.
rows.note: Failure modes differ: same-signed nodes lead to more OOB neurons, mixed-sign nodes to more interior minima.
rows.check: Changing teacher readout signs measures teacher-structure dependence, without a reported matched-width trend or extra-neuron comparison.

rows.subject: student networks on teachers with parallel hyperplanes
rows.operation_detail: Compared perfectly parallel minimally dissimilar teachers (θ = 0) with the non-parallel case.
rows.measure: Student success rate at reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Minimally dissimilar non-parallel teachers; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: The success rate is higher for perfectly parallel teachers than for the non-parallel case.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars represent standard error of the binomial proportion in Figure 14; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors attribute the reduction in interior minima to symmetry; OOB neurons occur at a higher rate.
rows.check: The fixed-width parallel-hyperplane comparison measures geometry dependence, not either width effect in V2.

rows.subject: student networks with differential parameter learning rates
rows.size_stated: ρ = 1; M = 4, D = 2 for minima-type comparison
rows.operation_detail: Increased readout weight and bias learning speed while decreasing inner-bias learning speed; also tested changes in each direction.

conditions.value: readout weights sped up and inner bias slowed down
10x example means readout weight and bias speed increased by 10 and inner bias speed decreased by 10

rows.measure: Percentage of student networks reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Equal learning rates; exact rate not stated.
rows.value: Success rates increase when readout learning rate is increased and decrease when inner-bias learning rate is increased.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in Figure 6A; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors state corresponding OOB neuron counts decrease or increase; Figure 6B shows minima-type frequencies.
rows.check: Differential parameter learning speeds do not test V5's stability-threshold claim. Figure 6A jointly speeds readout weights/bias and slows inner biases, so its curve alone cannot isolate their individual causal contributions.

rows.subject: student networks optimized with Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam with gradient flow for the three teacher distributions.
rows.measure: Fraction of students reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Gradient flow; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: Changing from gradient flow to Adam does not increase success rates; additional results are described as qualitatively similar.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in Figure 6C; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The paper says Adam does not prevent neurons from going out of bounds.
rows.check: The fixed-width Adam comparison does not test V2's width dependence; shallow regression also does not test V1's convolutional classification claim.

rows.subject: single-neuron student networks
rows.stage_stated: student initialized at specified angle; finite-data gradient flow
rows.operation_detail: Varied initial angle between student and teacher weights.

conditions.value: 20 linearly spaced values between 0 and π

rows.measure: Success rate at reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Initial angle 0; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: Success depends strongly on starting similarity; distant initializations are driven out of bounds.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in figures; exact values not stated.
rows.note: A separate stated result says no students with the opposite readout sign succeeded, regardless of starting angle (Figure 15B).
rows.check: A single-neuron initial-angle sweep does not test V4's activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.

rows.subject: single-neuron student networks
rows.stage_stated: opposite student and teacher readout signs; gradient flow
rows.operation_detail: Measured convergence for opposite-sign student-teacher systems across initial angles.
rows.measure: Success rate at reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Same-sign student-teacher systems; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: None of the students were successful, regardless of starting angle.
rows.check: Zero success for opposite-sign single-neuron initializations is correctly reported, but it does not measure any named version.

rows.subject: single-neuron student networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied input dimensionality while sampling student weights from the Glorot distribution.
rows.measure: Success rate at reaching the global minimum
rows.baseline: Other tested dimensionalities; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: Success rates show a slight positive trend as dimensionality increases.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in Figure 15C; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The text characterizes the differences as slight.
rows.check: Correct size_stated: D varies over {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}, rather than being fixed at 2. The dimensionality sweep does not compare initialization schemes or test V4.

rows.subject: single-neuron student networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied the teacher neuron bias (kink position).
rows.measure: Convergence rate to the global minimum
rows.baseline: Other tested bias settings; exact rates not stated.
rows.value: Convergence rates are higher when the ReLU kink is earlier, corresponding to more activated input space; differences are relatively slight for one node.
rows.uncertainty: Standard error of the binomial proportion shown in Figure 16; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The authors say the larger differences in the main results arise primarily from interactions between factors.
rows.check: The measure is the fraction reaching the global minimum, not temporal convergence speed. The teacher-bias sweep does not test a named version.
